value: A charity writes: “We run food banks that give free groceries to families in our county who cannot afford food.” Which statement is this, in Scrum.org's terms?
reason: “So that no family goes to bed hungry” reads as a long-term aspiration, so Vision Statement is also defensible; the new wording states only present purpose.

value: A team changed its sign-up form two weeks ago and has collected sign-up data every day since. Which Experiment Loop step comes next?
reason: “Changed last week” and “two weeks of data” contradict each other.

value: Besides the Product Owner, which Scrum accountability does the Nexus Integration Team include?
reason: “Has one holder on” is hard to parse; the Nexus Guide (p. 5) simply lists “a Scrum Master” as a member.

value: The hospital group tracks “income from private patients rose 8%”. Which EBM category of measure is this?
reason: “The trust’s” is NHS jargon a newcomer may not link to the hospital group.

value: Which Product Vision technique on Scrum.org has a team write about an imagined future, and is also called Newspaper Headline or Cover Story?
reason: The saved copy says only that participants “envision a future where…” (cut off); “the product already out in the world” is not supported.

value: B and C describe rules the Guide does not contain: the Scrum Master does not approve features, and the Guide does not restrict backlog changes to the Sprint Retrospective.
reason: “The backlog can be changed at any time” is not stated in the Scrum Guide.

value: The benefit a product gives its customers, and what the organization gains from it, in money or benefit to society.
reason: Scrum.org says the benefit is to “a customer”; “the people who use it” leaves out buyers.

value: Users can respond sooner, so the team learns and changes course sooner.
